In `LegacyCustomerDirectory.list(String sortBy, boolean descending)`, the check `!ALLOWED_SORT_KEYS.contains(sortBy)` was used.
If `sortBy` is `null`, `ALLOWED_SORT_KEYS.contains(null)` returns `false`, so `!false` is `true`, and it *should* throw `IllegalArgumentException`.

Wait, looking at the code I provided in the previous turn:
```java
    public List<String> list(String sortBy, boolean descending) {
        if (!ALLOWED_SORT_KEYS.contains(sortBy)) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Invalid sort key: " + sortBy);
        }
        // ...
    }
```
Wait, `Set.of(...)` creates a set that *does not* allow nulls.
Calling `ALLOWED_SORT_KEYS.contains(null)` on a `Set` created by `Set.of()` throws a `NullPointerException` in Java.

Ah, that's the problem. I need to handle the `null` case for `sortBy` explicitly before calling `.contains()`.

Corrected logic for `list`:
```java
    public List<String> list(String sortBy, boolean descending) {
        if (sortBy == null || !ALLOWED_SORT_KEYS.contains(sortBy)) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Invalid sort key: " + sortBy);
        }
        // ...
    }
```

Let's double check other methods for similar `null` issues.
`findByName(String name)`: `if (name == null) throw ...` - OK.
`searchByNamePrefix(String prefix)`: `if (prefix == null) throw ...` - OK.
`getById(String id)`: `validateId(id)` checks for `null` - OK.
`findByIds(List<String> ids)`: `if (ids == null) throw ...` and then loops and calls `validateId(id)` which checks for `null` - OK.
`richerThan(String minBalanceCents)`: `validateAmount(minBalanceCents)` checks for `null` - OK.
`sameCityAs(String id)`: `validateId(id)` checks for `null` - OK.
`deleteByCity(String city)`: `if (city == null) throw ...` - OK.

So the only issue is the `Set.of` `contains(null)` call.

Wait, let me verify the `Set.of` behavior.
In Java 9+, `Set.of` creates an immutable set. `Set.of("a", "b").contains(null)` throws `NullPointerException`.

Okay, I will fix that in `LegacyCustomerDirectory`.
